_readme: Drives kerzie.ai/swingbays/build (src/app/swingbays/build/route.ts), the INTERNAL Swing Bays project page for Wade, Jordan and Aaron. Password-gated (env SWINGBAYS_BUILD_PASSWORD), noindex, not in the sitemap or llms files. Edit this JSON, never the markup. Recipe: Wade OS clients/swing_bays/README_build_page.md. Rules: plain language, no em or en dashes, never the a-word for AI (name the AI or say 'the AI'), never a phone number or email, nothing we would not want Dustin to read if the link leaked (the password is the gate, the JSON is still factual). Seeded 2026-10-12 from the GHL build plan (ghl_build_plan_2026-10-12.md), the PSA cover page draft (10/7, revised 10/12), the repo transfer plan (10/12), the social inventory (10/1) and the 66-item plan.

_schema.clock_start: YYYY-MM-DD or null. Day 1 of the 90 = Parker go-live. Day 30/60/90 milestones compute from it.
_schema.milestones[]: key, label, date (YYYY-MM-DD) or offset (days from clock_start), approx (true = 'week of')
_schema.people[]: key, name, role, org, side ('us' or 'them')
_schema.items[]: id, workstream (key), kind (question | task | access | decision), text, from (person key who answers or provides), owner (person key who chases it), status (open | asked | answered | done | blocked), due (YYYY-MM-DD or null), answer (text once answered), source (where the item or the answer came from), updated (YYYY-MM-DD), step_one (true if Step One waits on it)

milestones.label: Walkthrough with Dustin, Shawn, Colter and Jordan: the plan, the timeline, what to expect
Signing target: PSA signed, first payment, Day 1 of the build
A2P texting registration submitted (Day 1 or 2; approval takes 1 to 3 weeks)
Jordan on site in Parker with Colter: forwarding, training, invitations prepped
November 1 invitations go out: email plus the social countdown
Reminders to the registered, final push to everyone else
Jordan back on site around the Day 30 hand-off
Day 30: Colter starts running it, we watch, oversee and guide
Day 60: check-in on the record, the answering and the posts

people.name: Colter Meek
people.role: General Manager, Parker; our one point of contact

people.name: Wade Kerzie
people.role: Founder; GHL agency admin, signs for Kerzie AI

workstreams.title: Customer record + November 1 launch
workstreams.goal: Step One (Wade 10/12): every customer in one GHL record, then fill the November 1 Englewood launch. Signing Wed 10/14 leaves 18 days.

workstreams.title: Accounts and access
workstreams.goal: Every login, token, user seat and consent click we need, in whose name, by when.

workstreams.title: Voice answering
workstreams.goal: No call goes to voicemail again by Day 7: the Denver number, the knowledge base, the Voice AI, Comcast forwarding on no-answer and after hours.

workstreams.title: DMs and texting (A2P)
workstreams.goal: Instagram and Facebook DMs answered from the same knowledge base; texts join the moment the A2P registration clears.

workstreams.title: Content engine
workstreams.goal: The shared video folder, the brand file, captions and the weekly social run in GHL's social planner.

workstreams.title: SimHouse booking
workstreams.goal: Three answers from Keegan pick the route. Until then the AI hands out the booking link and takes the request. Never lets this block launch.

workstreams.title: Hand-over
workstreams.goal: The Swing Bays Mac and Claude plan, the repo landing on their machine, training, the Day 30 and Day 90 steps.

items.text: November 1 event details: start and end time, what happens during the event, any offer for people who come, and the capacity we are filling toward.
Who is invited: Parker customers, members, lesson students, corporate contacts, partners or press? One registration covers both stores (Wade 10/12).

Every contact list and where it lives today: the Square customer export, the members list, lesson students, Dustin's own contacts, Colter's own contacts. For each: how many, what fields, who exports it.
Website form and newsletter sign-ups: which tool holds them today, how many, and can they be exported with the date and the page they came from.
SimHouse customers and bookings: what customer data SimHouse holds (name, email, phone, visits) and how it exports, so it lands in the one record.
Consent, list by list: which contacts agreed to email, which opted in to texts. A Square receipt email is not consent to text. Texts go only to opted-in people once A2P clears.
Englewood page for the launch: address, opening hours, what the page should say and link to by November 1 (the registration link goes on it).
Build the registration page and form in GHL: one link, a source tag per channel so the dashboard shows where each sign-up came from, an instant confirmation email.
Import every list into the Swing Bays sub-account, dedupe, and tag each contact by source, store, member or not, and what they agreed to receive.
Draft the email sequence: announcement, reminder about a week out, last call two days out, day-of note. Every email links to the one registration page.
Approve each invitation email and each countdown post before it goes out (the System is set to ask).
Social countdown on Instagram and Facebook through GHL's social planner: posts plus Stories, with lesson clips and Englewood build-out photos Jordan captures on site.
Capture Englewood build-out photos and lesson clips on site for the countdown.
Registration dashboard: sign-ups by day and by source.
Week of 10/26: reminders to everyone registered; final push to everyone not yet registered. Texts only if A2P has cleared and only to opted-in contacts.
Swing Bays legal entity name and type, business address, and Dustin's title. Needed on the PSA cover page and the A2P brand registration (the EIN goes straight into the A2P form, never on this page).
Send the PSA for e-signature in GHL and void the unsigned 9/10 Back Cover agreement there first.

Look inside the GotaGuy GHL sub-account for a phone number, an A2P registration or contacts worth exporting, then delete it (UI only). Verified 10/12: GotaGuy's social accounts and scheduled posts live in the Kerzie AI Solutions sub-account, not this one.

Create the Swing Bays sub-account in GHL (stays under Kerzie AI's plan, Wade 10/12) and its Private Integration Token with Voice AI, Conversation AI, phone, calendars, social, media and knowledge base scopes. About two minutes, UI only.
Buy the Denver local number by API once the token exists.

Create the private swingbays-os repo under Kerzie AI's GitHub from Wade's OS template; Jordan gets write access on signing. Prompts, FAQs, the brand file and recipes live there and move to their Mac later.
Website: which platform it runs on, and a user login for Kerzie AI (the PSA has Customer adding Provider as a user on the website).

DNS for the email sending domain (a mail subdomain of theswingbays.com): who holds the domain, and will they add the records on Day 1. A fresh sub-account sending from GHL's shared domain lands in spam more often.
Square: add Kerzie AI as a user, so we can export the customer list now and connect the ready-text pay link later.
Meta: who is admin on the Swing Bays Facebook Page and the @theswingbays Instagram business account. That person clicks the consent that connects them to GHL (Meta requires a human click).
Comcast Business: the admin login, or Colter at the keyboard for the forwarding session during Jordan's visit.
The Swing Bays Mac server and the Claude plan, bought in Swing Bays' name: when. The PSA says by the first on-site visit; Wade expects it may not be day one. We build in our repo either way.
Flip kerzie.ai/swingbays/proposal to project mode the day Dustin signs: mode, signed date, delete the example rows, real statuses.

For the FAQ knowledge base, both stores: hours, bay prices, lesson prices, leagues, memberships (tiers and what they include), club repair prices and turnaround, events, policies (cancellation, walk-ins, groups, kids, food and drink).
What callers ask most today, what goes to voicemail now, and what the current greeting says.
The name and voice on the phone: how the AI introduces itself, which voice, and the tone Dustin wants.
Forwarding rules: which line forwards, the after-hours schedule by day, and who receives the transcript and notification after each AI call (email or text, which people).
Englewood's main line: is a number assigned yet, who the carrier is, and when it goes live. It is answered by the AI from opening day.
Build the knowledge base in GHL: FAQs written from what we know plus a crawl of theswingbays.com (the KB API takes FAQs and a crawl, not a file upload). Jordan fills the gaps from Colter.

Create the Voice AI agent by API on the Denver number, pointed at the knowledge base. First write proves the API route; fallback is Claude writes the prompt and Jordan pastes it in GHL (five minutes).
Comcast Business: forward the main line to the Denver number on no-answer and after hours (not all calls). Test from a cell phone: daytime no-answer, after close.
For the A2P registration: the opt-in line on the website forms, who receives the texts, and a sample of each kind of text we will send (ready text, booking confirmation, reminders, offers).
Draft every A2P brand and campaign field for Wade to submit. One registration covers both stores (Wade 10/12).
Submit the A2P brand and campaign in GHL on Day 1 or 2. Approval takes 1 to 3 weeks; texting waits on it, voice does not.
Who answers Instagram and Facebook DMs today, from which device, and what people ask most in DMs.
Who gets the hand-off when the AI cannot answer a DM or a text, and how (notification to which person).
Create the Conversation AI bot on the same knowledge base, Facebook and Instagram DMs first. SMS joins the moment A2P clears.
items.answer: Waits on the Meta consent click (access-10).

items.text: Website: a 'Text us 24/7' line instead of a chat bubble (Wade: people ignore the pop-ups). The web chat widget stays optional. Needs Dustin's yes and Shawn's hands.
Posting cadence: every day, or Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Dustin's call.
Where the daily lesson videos live today (camera roll, a personal Facebook profile, somewhere else) and whether Dustin and the instructors will save them to one shared iCloud folder.
items.source: ghl_build_plan 10/12; social inventory 10/1 (lesson videos not found on the brand Page)

items.text: Which instructors record lessons, and whether their videos post under the brand account, Dustin's own account, or both.

Set up the shared iCloud folder (shared to Wade's Apple ID during the build so Claude reads it on our Mac; their Mac reads the same folder after hand-over) and show Dustin and the instructors 'Save to Files' from the camera roll.
Brand kit files: logo files, colors, fonts, any voice or tone rules, and photo of the stores. Shawn built the site, so he likely holds them.
What Smitten Labs runs for Swing Bays marketing today (email tool, ads, posting, the newsletter) so our posts and emails do not collide with his.
One brand file in the repo (logo, colors, fonts, voice rules). It drives every caption, card and reply.

Which accounts post: the brand @theswingbays, Dustin's @dustinmillergolf, the Facebook Page. And whether to open the Swing Bays YouTube channel and TikTok now (both handles unclaimed as of 10/1) and who holds those logins.

The weekly social run, same recipe as GotaGuy's: pick lesson videos, burn on the caption, write the description, schedule to Instagram and Facebook in GHL's social planner. Their dashboard shows the post calendar.
Arrange the virtual session with Keegan before Jordan's first visit (PSA Customer Obligations: Customer arranges the SimHouse session).
Is there a SimHouse API, and what can it read and write.
Is there a calendar feed (iCal or Google), and does it sync both ways.
Can a booking be written into SimHouse from outside (by text or DM), and what a booking needs: bay, time, length, name, payment.
The booking link per store, and whether lessons book through SimHouse or somewhere else.
items.source: ghl_build_plan 10/12 (interim answer hands out the link)

items.text: Interim: the AI answers 'book a bay' with the SimHouse booking link and takes the request for staff (plan item 13).

Pick the connection route from Keegan's answers: (a) API, Claude writes the read/write connection; (b) calendar feed only, the Google calendar mirror (SimHouse to Google to GHL); (c) neither, Keegan shows how it is built and we write the connection. The AI checks availability against SimHouse, it does not own the booking.
Who sits at the cockpit besides Colter (Dustin, Brenna), and what each person should see on the dashboard.
Command center dashboard at one private web address on Kerzie AI's Vercel (interim hosting until their machine exists): post calendar, calls answered, DMs, repairs, bookings, new contacts.
Repo home at hand-over: Kerzie AI keeps swingbays-os with Swing Bays as admin (default, simpler for Right to Use updates), or transfer ownership. Transfer only if they end SOW 2.
Land on their machine: clone the repo, place the env file, sign in to their Claude, run the first session with Colter at the keyboard. On site, Denver.
items.answer: Waits on the Swing Bays Mac and Claude plan (access-12).

items.text: Staff training materials, the same for every store, in Swing Bays' voice. Run from their machine.
Day 30: Colter starts running it; Jordan on site around the week of November 16. Day 90: Colter signs off, acceptance window 10 business days.
